lessons.title: Electron-phonon DFPT needs norm-conserving UPFs in QE 7.6
lessons.text: QE 7.6's ph.x stopped with a segmentation fault in elphel (adddvscf) for electron-phonon runs with PAW UPFs. The same runs with norm-conserving UPFs (PseudoDojo) finished, for aluminium and niobium.

lessons.title: SSSP's Ga and As UPFs give wrong GaAs phonons
lessons.text: With SSSP's Ga and As UPFs, QE 7.6 gave GaAs an acoustic frequency of 118 cm-1 at Γ before the sum rule and transverse branches about 50 % above experiment (122 cm-1 at X), at a density cutoff of 560 or 1120 Ry and on shifted or denser meshes. PseudoDojo norm-conserving UPFs gave 50 cm-1 and branches within 11 cm-1 of ABINIT. Silicon with SSSP was fine.

lessons.title: A shifted mesh for GaAs's dielectric response
lessons.text: On a Γ-centred 8x8x8 mesh GaAs's electronic dielectric constant came out as 27-30, because the 0.5 eV PBE direct gap sits on a mesh point. The same mesh shifted by half a step along each axis (kshift 1 1 1) gave 13.6 and neutral Born charges, with SSSP or PseudoDojo UPFs.

lessons.title: Hybrid SCF: exchange threshold and pools
lessons.text: GaAs with HSE06 on a 6x6x6 mesh: the exchange error fell to about 1e-6 Ry within 5 outer iterations and then by only 10 % per iteration, levelling off near 1e-7 Ry, while the gap had settled at 1.379 eV. A 1e-8 Ry threshold did not finish in 2 hours; 1e-6 Ry finished in 1 h 38 min on 32 ranks. Sixteen pools instead of the two pw.x chose made the exchange slower.

lessons.title: Electron-phonon coupling and Tc of Al and Nb on coarse meshes
lessons.text: Through lambda.x and EPW 6.1 with μ* = 0.1: aluminium gave λ 0.44-0.46 (measured about 0.43) and an Eliashberg Tc of 2.5-3.0 K (measured 1.18 K); niobium gave λ 1.08-1.54 depending on the broadening, above the 1.0-1.2 of converged calculations, and Tc 18-22 K (measured 9.25 K). First Tc scans of 0.25-2 K and 1-14 K did not reach the transition; choose temperature ranges that bracket it.

lessons.title: Small negative α²F weights after Fourier interpolation
lessons.text: matdyn's interpolated α²F of aluminium had small negative weights below 6.8 meV for the narrowest of ten broadenings, 0.64 % of its λ. DFT Agent keeps a broadening whose negative weights stay within 1 % of λ, reports it, and excludes broadenings beyond that.

lessons.title: Lithium compounds need lradstp 2
lessons.text: Elk's lithium species keeps 1s in the valence. On the default coarse radial mesh (lradstp 4) LiF lost 0.2 % of its charge and the PBE SCF did not converge. Elk's own LiF examples use lradstp 2, and DFT Agent sets it whenever lithium is present.

lessons.title: LiF exciton with the bootstrap kernel
lessons.text: With a 5.2 eV scissor (the experimental 14.2 eV gap minus Elk's LDA gap of 8.97 eV, as in Elk's LiF bootstrap example), the bootstrap TDDFT kernel gave an exciton at 13.76 eV, below the 14.19 eV gap, with Im ε = 48. Without local fields the spectrum has no exciton and peaks at 16.6 eV (Elk 11.0.2 on Arrhenius).

lessons.title: Silicon dielectric function without local fields
lessons.text: Silicon without local fields gave its strongest absorption at 3.72 eV and Re ε(0) = 13.48. Fermi–Dirac smearing of a semiconductor produced an artefact in ε(0) (14.67) that DFT Agent's optics stage now avoids.

lessons.title: Laser demagnetization needs spin–orbit coupling and a zero-field reference
lessons.text: Real-time TDDFT on fcc Ni (6×6×6 mesh, 2.4 as steps): without spin–orbit coupling the total spin is conserved (+0.005 % after a 1 V/Å pulse). With it, a 2 V/Å, 1.55 eV pulse of 3 fs FWHM lowered the moment by 13.8 % in 15 fs, and it kept falling after the pulse. The same evolution without a field changed the moment by 5e-8 %, which shows the time step was short enough. Plan both runs.

lessons.title: Time evolution rewrites the ground-state files
lessons.text: Before time zero, Elk's time evolution (task 460) runs a static-field iteration that rewrites INFO.OUT, EFERMI.OUT and EIGVAL.OUT. Take ground-state results from the preceding SCF, not from the time-evolution folder.

lessons.title: Silicon phonons by DFPT agree with QE and experiment
lessons.text: Silicon (PBE, PseudoDojo norm-conserving, Γ-centred 8x8x8 k mesh, 4x4x4 q mesh, anaddb interpolation) gave 514.4 cm-1 at Γ (measured 517), X 140/410/462 and L 107/374/414/490 cm-1, within 1 cm-1 of QE on the same meshes. The electronic dielectric constant came out as 14.0 and the Born charges zero.

lessons.title: Small-gap semiconductors need dense meshes for dielectric response
lessons.text: GaAs on a Γ-centred 8x8x8 k mesh gave an electronic dielectric constant of 29.7 (measured about 11) and Born charges ±2.27 that missed charge neutrality by 0.27 e before it was imposed, so the LO-TO splitting was too small (LO 278 against 292 cm-1 measured). The 0.5 eV PBE direct gap at Γ sits on a mesh point. ABINIT stops on QE's half-step shifted fcc mesh (chksymbreak), so use a denser Γ-centred mesh; QE with a shifted mesh gave 13.6.

lessons.title: Metal phonons need a dense k mesh and broadening
lessons.text: Aluminium phonons by DFPT with a 16x16x16 k mesh and 0.27 eV broadening reached 315 cm-1 at the top of the spectrum (measured 323). A 12x12x12 mesh gave a highest frequency 7 % higher.

lessons.title: Spin-orbit gaps agree with QE
lessons.text: With fully relativistic PseudoDojo pseudopotentials (PBE), ABINIT's spin-orbit gaps of GaAs (0.411 eV) and monolayer MoS2 (1.617 eV) matched QE's to 1 meV on the same meshes.

lessons.title: Large insulating cells: Γ point with orbital transformation
lessons.text: With orbital transformation at Γ, a 512-atom silicon cell converged in 2.5 minutes on 128 cores and a 1000-atom cell in 4.2 minutes on 256 cores (CP2K 2026.2 on Arrhenius); their energies per atom differ by 2 meV. Use a supercell rather than a k-point mesh for such systems; metals need diagonalization with smearing instead.

lessons.title: Liquid water: equilibrate before the production run
lessons.text: A packed 64-molecule water box released 10 eV in its first 25 fs and stayed near 397 K; relaxing the box did not reach 0.05 eV/Å in 200 steps. A 200 fs MD stage under a 10 fs CSVR thermostat held 312 ± 10 K, and the following 1 ps run from its final frame held 294 ± 15 K (conserved-energy drift 0.07 meV/atom/ps, O–O peak 2.725 Å), but its potential energy was still falling over the second half. A packed box needs several picoseconds before averages are equilibrium values.
